title: `voids/vitality-form-void` reads a differential fMRI contrast as absence ("The dimension appeared when the task asked for it and not otherwise … a mind running the default *what* task never meets the *how*"), although its own reference 3 (Di Cesare et al. 2019) found the insular sector active under a *what* instruction and called recognition automatic; and it cites the autism dissociation to Di Cesare, Bruschetta et al. (2024), whose Introduction is summarising Rochat et al. (2013) and whose own finding is that autistic children can convey gentle and rude forms
